chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Mu'awiya and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the substance of al-usrubb (a type of coin), which, when refined, contains silver. Is it permissible for a man to pay the named dirhams using it? He said: 'If the dominant name upon it is al-usrubb, then there is no harm with that,' meaning it is known only as al-usrubb.

key_terms.الدَّرَاهِمَ: Dirhams, silver coins used as currency.
key_terms.الْأُسْرُبِّ: Al-usrubb, a specific type of coin mentioned in the text.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using a local or distinct coin for payment if it is known by a name other than 'dirham'?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Shia juristic principle of *al-ism al-dalil* (naming as evidence), where the prevailing common name of a currency dictates its legal classification for transactions like *salam* (advance payment). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that despite the coin's silver content, its distinct identity as 'al-usrubb' exempts it from the strict regulations governing standard dirhams, highlighting the importance of social convention (*urf*) in Islamic commercial law. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia fiqh in adapting to the evolving monetary systems of the time.
